extracted.intended_audience: trademark applicants, holders, representatives/agents, and national/regional IP Offices using the Madrid System
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and legal requirements and procedural rules for filing, prosecuting, managing and recording international trademark registrations under the Madrid Protocol, aimed at applicants, holders, their representatives and IP Offices. Covers substantive eligibility, application content, procedural time limits, fees, communications, examination/refusal procedures, post-registration changes and accession requirements for Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who May Use the System?
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria defining entitlement to use the Madrid System (who can file an international application through the Office of Origin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that use of the System is limited to entitled persons (owners of a basic application or basic registration in the Office of Origin or other categories established by the Protocol/Regulations) and discusses selecting entitlement and Office of Origin (see 'Entitlement and the Office of Origin'). Also covers several applicants and representation implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic Application or Registration (the Basic Mark)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international registration must be based on a 'basic application' or 'basic registration' (the Basic Mark).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details how the international application depends on the basic application/registration (including dependency period), selection of the basic mark, requirements for identity/consistency with the basic filing, and consequences if the basic application/registration is amended, refused, or cancelled (dependency effects discussed elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement and the Office of Origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to claim entitlement and to file the international application through an Office of Origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on choosing entitlement and Office of Origin, and practical implications for filing (e.g., Office of Origin must certify/counter-sign and issue required certification/signature). Discusses cases with several applicants and entitlement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Several Applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and content rules when an international application is filed in the names of more than one applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how names/addresses, signatures and representation must be handled for multiple applicants and how offices record multiple holders; see application form and recording rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of the International Application
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must be presented in the prescribed form and manner (generally via the Office of Origin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers presentation options, required fields on the form, use of eMadrid online forms, certification/signature by Office of Origin, and practical tips for completing form fields (applicant details, mark, goods/services, designations, fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of the International Application / Trilingual Regime
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements on language(s) acceptable for international applications, communications and the 'trilingual regime'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies permitted filing languages, notes the trilingual regime and how languages affect filings, notifications, translations, and records. Also references language requirements for subsequent communications and publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Application Form — Applicant’s Details and Other Indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory and optional applicant details on the application form (name, address, e‑mail, alternative postal address, phone, preferred correspondence language, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains each data field, significance (e.g., e-mail mandatory), how alternative addresses function, and implications for notifications and communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory E-mail Address for Applicants, Holders and Representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants, holders and representatives must provide an e‑mail address for communications with the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the mandatory nature of e‑mail contact details, explains where it must be provided (application, requests), and the role of e‑mail in electronic communications and notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and Effect of a Representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for appointment, recording, notification, change and cancellation of a representative; only one representative may be recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on how to appoint a representative (in application or separate form), consequences/effect of appointment, recording by IB, change notifications, irregular appointments, cancellation procedures, no fee for recording, and obligations/limitations of representation (including e‑mail requirement of representative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Only One Representative
rubrics_metrics.description: At any one time only one representative may be recorded before the International Bureau for an international registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the 'only one representative' rule, practical consequences (how to change/replace), and how Offices and holders should manage representation changes and notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Signature requirements for applicants, holders, representatives and certification by the Office of Origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes where and how signatures must appear (applicant/representative signature on application or form, certification/signature of the international application by the Office of Origin), acceptable signature modalities and consequences of missing/irregular signatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Mark — Special Kinds (Three-dimensional, Sound, Collective, Certification or Guarantee Marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific requirements and indications for special kinds of marks when filing an international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to present and describe special marks, necessary supplementary information (e.g., reproductions, descriptions, technical data), and how Offices may treat non-standard marks in the international registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark in Color, Color Claims and Standard Characters
rubrics_metrics.description: How to claim color(s) in an international application and how standard character marks are treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on indicating which parts of the mark are in color, how to claim color(s) (including when basic mark is B/W), and implications for reproduction and scope of protection; discusses marks consisting exclusively of color or combinations of colors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transliteration and Translation of the Mark
rubrics_metrics.description: Transliteration of the mark is mandatory; translation is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States transliteration must be provided; translation may be provided optionally. Explains where to include transliteration/translation in the application and implications for publication and examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of the Mark, Verbal Elements and Disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional and mandatory elements to describe the mark and provide verbal elements or disclaimers as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples of verbal-element statements, how to draft voluntary descriptions or disclaimers, and how these affect interpretation/examination by Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goods and Services — List, Limitation and Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for listing goods and services, limitations, proper classification, and consequences of irregularities in the list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to prepare a goods/services list (use of Madrid Goods and Services Manager recommended), rules on limitation of goods/services, acceptable specificity, classification rules, common irregularities (e.g., imprecise terms) and how they must be remedied (by Office of Origin or applicant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependency Period
rubrics_metrics.description: The international registration may depend on the basic application/registration for a fixed period (dependency period) during which revocation/cancellation of the basic filing can affect the international registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the length and effect of the dependency period, examples of dependency consequences, and strategies (e.g., subsequent designation, conversion) to manage dependency risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑filing Searches and Examination Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations to conduct pre‑filing searches and overview that designated Offices will examine according to their national/regional practices and grounds for refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises applicants to conduct searches before filing to assess registrability and risk; summarizes that Offices examine under their national law and may issue provisional refusals based on grounds such as absolute/relative grounds, conflicts, descriptiveness, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irregularities in the International Application and How They Are Handled
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of irregularities (classification, indication of goods/services, missing data) and whether they must be remedied by the Office of Origin or the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classifies irregularities and states whether IB will require Office of Origin to correct them, or will invite the applicant to remedy; gives examples and practical procedures for cure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of the International Application by the International Bureau (Irregularities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau examines the international application for formal irregularities and records/publication issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists irregularities the IB checks (classification, indication of goods/services, signature, fees), procedures for inviting remedies, treatment of irregular notifications, and the effect on date of international registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of International Application and Subsequent Designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules establishing the date of the international application and for the date of subsequent designations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how dates are determined (receipt, certification, payment), special cases affecting date, and consequences for priority and rights (including examples for subsequent designation close to renewal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of Fees — Types, Calculation, Currency and Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on applicable fees (complementary/supplementary/standard fees, individual fees), how to calculate them, currency of payment, and permitted payment methods (debit from current account, credit card, online payment, others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes fee categories, fee calculation sheet, individual vs standard fee regimes, fee reductions for LDC applicants, payment modes, date of payment, partial payments (fee payable in two parts), change in amount of fee, and practical instructions (use online fee calculator and payment systems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee Reduction for Applicants from Least Developed Countries (LDCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision for reduction of fees for applicants from LDCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains eligibility for reduced fees, how the reduction is applied, and which fees it covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued Processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure and conditions for continued processing of an application when time limits are missed or irregularities exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes when continued processing is available, required requests/forms, effects on date and processing, and interplay with relief measures and excuse in delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Limits and Relief Measures; Excuse in Delay in Meeting Time Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on procedural time limits (filing, response to provisional refusals, communications) and relief measures/excuse in delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains general time limits, options to extend or excuse delays, conditions for relief, who may request relief (applicant/Office), and how relief interacts with national time limits set by Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration, Recording and Publication of the International Registration
rubrics_metrics.description: How the international registration is recorded, content of the International Register and publication rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what the IB records and publishes (content of registration), language of registration/publication, extract and legalization of extracts, and how publications appear in the WIPO Gazette of International Marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of the International Registration; Period of Validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal effects conferred by an international registration and its period of validity (renewal, duration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that international registration produces effects equivalent to national registration in designated members (subject to examination/refusal), standard period of protection (10 years) and renewal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for Refusal by Designated Members
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive and procedural grounds on which a designated Office may refuse protection of an international registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies that Offices may refuse based on their national law (absolute and relative grounds), non-entitlement, conflicts with prior rights, descriptiveness, misleading marks, etc.; references detailed grounds and examples in the Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Limits for Refusal and Extension Possibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limits for designated Offices to notify provisional refusal (generally one year, possible extension to 18 months or more by declaration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the standard 12‑month refusal period, the possibility for a member to declare 18 months (or set other extensions, especially for oppositions), how such declarations are made (instrument of accession or later) and when they take effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for Refusal of Protection and Notification of Provisional Refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal procedure Offices must follow to notify provisional refusals and the required content of notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details how a provisional refusal is notified through the IB, required language, form and content, how provisional refusals are recorded and published, and remedies available to holders (response, opposition procedures, requests for additional information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Limit to Respond to a Provisional Refusal; Total or Partial Refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Time allowed to the holder to respond to a provisional refusal and the possibility of total or partial refusals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies response timeframes set by the designated Office, effects of no timely response, and how partial refusals (for specific goods/services) are handled; discusses conditional acceptance options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Refusal Based on Opposition and Conditional Acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: How oppositions at national level may give rise to provisional refusals and the concept of conditional acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that where domestic opposition procedures result in refusal, an Office may notify a provisional refusal and may also issue conditional acceptances; clarifies interaction between local opposition processing and international procedure timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and Publication of Provisional Refusal; Language of Notification
rubrics_metrics.description: How provisional refusals (regular or irregular) are recorded/published and the language requirements for notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes whether irregular provisional refusals are recorded, cases where provisional refusal is not regarded as such, rectification possibilities, language of the notification and how irregular notifications are treated by the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of a Mark in a Designated Member (Interim Status, Final Status, Statements of Grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and procedures regarding interim status, final status and statements of grant of protection where no provisional refusal is communicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains interim status during the refusal period, final status upon grant of protection, issuance of statements of grant of protection when no provisional refusal is communicated, and how these statuses are recorded and communicated to the holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further Decisions Affecting the Scope of Protection and Recording under Rule 18ter
rubrics_metrics.description: How further decisions by designated members affect scope of protection and the recording of such decisions (Rule 18ter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details procedures for recording statements concerning scope or refusal of protection, subsequent decisions affecting scope, and notification/recording of these decisions in the International Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation in a Designated Member and Recording of Invalidations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds and procedures for national invalidation of protection and how invalidations are recorded in the International Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains national invalidation processes, recording requirements, effect on international registration and notification to the holder and IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications from the Offices of Designated Members Under Rule 23bis
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural channel and content requirements for communications from Offices to the holder via the IB under Rule 23bis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the kinds of communications that flow under Rule 23bis, how they are transmitted, and the effects and recording of such communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent Designation — Presentation, Language, Content and Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for presenting a subsequent designation (when adding new designated members after the original international registration), language requirements, official form content and legal effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to present subsequent designations (forms, fee calculation), language and signature rules, indication of goods/services, voluntary descriptions, declaration of intention to use, and consequences (date of subsequent designation, period of protection, limits when near renewal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of Various Changes in the International Registration (Name, Address, Legal Nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and requirements to record changes in the holder’s name, address or legal nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies official forms, required indications (international registration number, name of holder), signature requirements, office of the member presenting the request, fee calculation sheet, irregular request handling and effects of recording such changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of a Limitation, Renunciation and Cancellation — Effects and Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: How to present requests to record limitation, renunciation or cancellation of an international registration and the legal effects of recording such acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes content of requests (official form), which international registrations are concerned, signature and holder requirements, designated members affected, fee issues (limitation only), irregular requests and recording/notification/publication consequences, and how a recorded restriction takes effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in Ownership — Entitlement of the Transferee to Be the New Holder
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements to record change in ownership and the entitlement assessment for the transferee to become the new holder of an international registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains documentation required (assignment instruments, evidence of entitlement), signature and form requirements, Office presenting request, fee implications, and recording/notification procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of Intention to Use the Mark (Member Notification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members may notify the Director General that they require a declaration of intention to use the mark whenever designated under the Protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how this notification may be made (instrument of accession or later), when it takes effect (three months after receipt or later date), and that it may be withdrawn at any time (effect upon receipt or later date indicated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration That Recording of Licenses in the International Register Has No Effect
rubrics_metrics.description: An Office may notify that recording of trademark licenses in the International Register has no effect in that member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when such declarations may be made (either at any time if legislation does not provide for recording or before the date of becoming bound if legislation does provide but Office chooses to notify no effect), and that the declaration may be withdrawn later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations Concerning Division and Merger of an International Registration
rubrics_metrics.description: An Office may notify WIPO whether it will present requests for division or merger of international registrations, depending on whether national law provides for division/merger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that if national law does not provide for division/merger, the Office may notify it will not present such requests; such notifications must be received before becoming bound by the Protocol; notifications may be withdrawn later with consequences for holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Fees — Members May Demand Individual Fees Instead of Standard Fee Share
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member may declare that it wishes to receive an 'individual fee' in connection with each international registration/designation and renewal instead of participating in the standard fee regime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets conditions for making the declaration (useful where local fees exceed 100 CHF equivalent), the requirement that individual fee not exceed the national fee for 10 years after deduction of international savings, how declaration is made (instrument of accession or later) and interaction with Article 9sexies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of Time Limit for Notifying Provisional Refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Members may declare that the time limit for their Office to notify a provisional refusal shall be 18 months instead of one year (and may allow notification after 18 months in certain opposition cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains declaration timing (instrument of accession or later), when it comes into effect (three months after receipt), and that such extensions should be considered in accession planning and applicant strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparations for Accession — Initial and Second Assessment, Road Map and Accession Team
rubrics_metrics.description: For Offices preparing to accede to the Protocol: requirements to conduct initial assessments across six areas, set up an Accession Team, establish a detailed Road Map and carry out a second assessment/desk audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the six main areas to assess (change leadership; legislation; organizational/institutional; procedural/operational; IT/automation; community changes), what information to provide (political will, export industry, agents, timetable), composition and role of Accession Team, and the purpose of the Road Map and second assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislation — Madrid‑compatible National Trademark Law Required Prior to Accession
rubrics_metrics.description: An accession candidate must have functioning trademark legislation complying with the Paris Convention and be able to implement Madrid‑compatible provisions before accession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States Madrid‑compatible legislation must be in place before accession to ensure holders can enforce rights; WIPO can assist with draft provisions and legal assistance; discusses compliance checks and sample model provisions available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational, Procedural, IT and Community Requirements for Accession
rubrics_metrics.description: IP Office must ensure appropriate organizational structure, staffing/training, reliable domestic procedures, IT systems and stakeholder awareness before accession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details organizational topics to consider (language(s), institutional strength, staffing and training, examination system/time limits, fee structure, statistics), procedural integration with Madrid processes, IT readiness for electronic communications and automation, and community outreach to industry and agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accession Instrument Deposit and Effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure and timing for accession: deposit of instrument of accession with Director General of WIPO; Protocol enters into effect three months after receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains who usually signs (Head of State or Foreign Affairs Minister), the option to submit declarations upon deposit, and when declarations come into effect; notes WIPO will advise on declaration options.
